architecture_principles: a discovered material regularity is only usable inside the chemistry family in which it was measured
a scientific applicability boundary is executable code, not prompt advice
the language model may criticize the rule and may not override it
value of information is computed by a deterministic tool over the admissible set only
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
every gate decision carries a machine-readable reason and is serialized with the run

arm_difference_declaration.forbidden_confound: Hiding applicability information from V5_NO_GATE while showing it to V5_FULL is prohibited by protocol v1.1.
held_identical: model endpoint and stage model assignment
evidence access profile and filtered evidence state
raw assess_shared_shape_applicability outputs for every candidate
the full inadmissible-card list and its machine-readable reasons
VOI implementation, weights and tie epsilon
arm_difference_declaration.information_parity_evidence: build_pre_enforcement_payload() takes no arm argument, and its SHA-256 is written into every run as pre_enforcement_payload_sha256. The two arms must report the same hash.
arm_difference_declaration.only_intended_difference: whether the identical chemistry-domain applicability audit is enforced as hard experiment-card admissibility before VOI and at freeze
arm_difference_declaration.payload_consequence: Both arms receive the same audit, the same per-candidate applicability outputs and the same inadmissible-card list. V5_NO_GATE marks the audit advisory and keeps every card selectable; V5_FULL marks it binding and removes the inadmissible cards from the ranked set.

candidate_space.rationale: V5 reuses the byte-identical V3/V4 lattice so that the measured change is the chemistry-domain constraint, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> mandatory chemistry-audited local science tool -> deterministic chemistry-domain applicability audit (identical and model-visible in both arms) -> enforcement (V5_FULL only) -> VOI over the selectable set -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze

rules: M-HOLD-120 is admissible: it measures thermal-hold drift directly and does not use the shared thermal-response shape.
M-REPEAT is admissible: it measures realization/state spread directly.
M-SWEEP is admissible: it is the direct verification measurement for a chemistry-shifted candidate.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use equal to allowed_with_state_anchor, or when configs/verified_shape_transfer.json records a completed direct sweep for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification. This is deterministic inadmissibility, not a VOI penalty and not prompt advice.

architecture.claim_boundary: V5.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime with a deterministic chemistry-domain admissibility constraint. A V5 result is evidence about executable scientific constraints on measurement choice. It is not a wet-lab result and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.manuscript_boundary: V5 run results must not be written into manuscript/MAIN_TEXT_V5.md or manuscript/SUPPLEMENTARY_INFORMATION_V5.md until the run series is audited and explicitly frozen by the author.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_CHEMISTRY_GATED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V5
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information or admissibility
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
re-running, rewriting or reinterpreting the frozen V4 series

primary_arms.role: advice-only control isolating the incremental effect of turning identical scientific applicability information into an executable hard constraint
prospective chemistry-aware Agent V5 with executable scientific constraints

architecture.purpose: Test whether an experimentally discovered material regularity and its chemistry-domain boundary can be executed as a hard scientific constraint on which measurement an outcome-blind Agent is allowed to select.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question the next experiment must answer, and request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations
execute read-only scientific tools. The chemistry-audited local rheology summary is mandatory and is forced into the trace whether or not the planner requested it.

deterministic, non-LLM measurement-applicability audit. Computed once per run without reference to the arm, fully visible to the model in both arms, serialized in full, and never produced by a model stage.
V5_FULL only. Converts the identical audit into hard admissibility before VOI ranking and again at freeze. It cannot be overridden by any model stage.
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value from the cards present in the payload
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability and whether its falsification criterion can actually be met
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported weight sensitivity and the strongest objection
commit to one experiment card present in the payload, or abstain, and state its acceptance and falsification criteria
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card. A selection outside the admissible set is rejected at freeze rather than repaired.

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V5 is a new prospective runtime. configs/agent_v4.json, scripts/run_agent_v4.py, prompts/agent_v4_*.txt, src/pur_new/voi.py and every frozen V3/V4 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V5.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards

decision_stability_sent_to_model.evaluated_over: the selectable experiment cards of this arm
decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Accept the low-drift acrylic-only outcome if the arithmetic mean SI_15_60 across at least two independent preparations is below 3.80%. This is below half of the frozen 7.61% linear-dilution prediction for reactive mass fraction 0.8000 and supports H-RESIN while falsifying H-CORE and the tackifier-required prediction of H-DUAL.
judge_normalized.chemistry_support_statement: S1C49 is acrylic-modified chemistry outside the family in which the shared temperature-response shape was measured. However, the selected primary observable is measured directly at 120 C and does not depend on any rheological regularity measured in the same chemistry family, shared-shape transfer, model fit, or one-point reconstruction. The experiment can therefore support only a formulation-level hold-drift claim; it cannot support temperature-response transfer or a molecular mechanism.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: If mean SI_15_60 is at or above 7.61%, falsify H-RESIN for S1C49; that outcome remains compatible with H-CORE and H-DUAL and does not separate them. If mean SI_15_60 is below 3.80%, falsify H-CORE and H-DUAL. A mean from 3.80% inclusive to below 7.61% falsifies none of the three registered hypotheses under the frozen thresholds.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: If H-RESIN is falsified by SI_15_60 at or above 7.61%, run S1C41::M-HOLD-120 under the same controlled and recorded preparation history. The matched-reactive-fraction dual-axis formulation then tests whether adding 5% TK100 produces the low-drift regime absent from acrylic-only S1C49.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: Arithmetic mean across at least two independent preparations of SI_15_60 = 100 × (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, measured directly during the 120 C hold; individual-repeat SI_15_60 values and their range must also be reported.
judge_normalized.rationale: S1C49::M-HOLD-120 is admissible under the binding chemistry audit and directly measures the declared failure mode. Its principal value is discrimination: low acrylic-only drift separates H-RESIN from the tackifier-required H-DUAL prediction, which none of the deterministic top dual-axis cards can do. The conclusion is limited to formulation-level rheological behavior.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I follow the Robustness Adjudicator rather than the Proposer and deterministic tied-top ranking. The Proposer's S1C41 dual-axis card has higher ranked VOI and minimum burden within its tie, but it leaves H-RESIN and H-DUAL entangled. S1C49 is the matched-reactive-fraction acrylic-only probe and can formally falsify H-DUAL if low drift occurs without TK100. I also adopt the Skeptic's warning that the E1-derived 7.61% baseline does not uniquely establish H-CORE versus H-RESIN without an unmodified E2-core hold.

uncertainty_decomposition.evidence_coverage_uncertainty: No unmodified E2-core hold baseline is available, so the 7.61% comparator transfers the single-run E1 drift coefficient from NCO:OH 1.7 to an E2-derived core at NCO:OH 1.8. Consequently, deviation from 7.61% is informative under the frozen registry but cannot uniquely attribute suppression relative to a directly measured E2 baseline.
uncertainty_decomposition.extrapolation_uncertainty: The 20% acrylic-only composition is within the stated externally supported acrylic region, but the modified chemistry has no verified local shared-shape transfer. This does not invalidate direct M-HOLD-120 drift measurement, but it prohibits thermal-shape or anchor-reconstruction claims without a fresh M-SWEEP.
uncertainty_decomposition.measurement_uncertainty: The declared matched-window drift discrimination threshold is 2.00 percentage points. At least two independent preparations are required, with the arithmetic mean used for adjudication and all individual SI_15_60 values reported; the E1 reference underlying 7.61% came from only one hold run.
uncertainty_decomposition.realization_state_uncertainty: E2 realizations showed 2.80-3.57-fold viscosity-scale spreads, including 3.57-fold at 120 C. Preparation and hold histories must therefore be controlled and recorded. The relative-drift observable reduces, but does not eliminate, this state confounding.

planner.chemistry_support_statement: The local thermal-response regularities were measured in the original reactive PUR formulation family represented by E1, E2 and E3, with original hold evidence from E1 and E5; E1 +P is a separately verified chemical perturbation rather than part of the primary same-composition fit. The intended experiment remains anchored to the E2 reactive core but introduces acrylic-like and potentially minor tackifier-like modifiers, so it does not automatically remain inside the chemistry support of the measured shared thermal shape. Applicability must be audited for each modified candidate, with a direct temperature sweep required when support is not established.
planner.failure_mode: Excessive viscosity growth during prolonged melt residence at 120 C, with unresolved formulation dependence of thermal-hold drift.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original E5 thermal hold showed SI_15_60 = 0.5154, corresponding to a 51.54% viscosity increase from 15 to 60 min at 120 C; by contrast, E1 increased 9.51% over the same window. Each reported hold trajectory is only a single run.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Only E1 and E5 have original 120 C hold trajectories, each represented by one four-point run over 15-90 min. This is much sparser than the 80-130 C temperature-response data and provides no repeat estimate for the primary 15-60 min drift observable. The E2 reactive-core anchor itself has no reported hold trajectory in the filtered evidence.
measurement_requirements: Use the matched-window M-HOLD-120 protocol: hold at 120 C, measure viscosity at 15, 30, 45 and 60 min, and report SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 as a percent without extrapolating beyond the measured window.
Run at least two independent preparations per composition under controlled and recorded process histories so that the 2 percentage-point drift discrimination threshold can be evaluated.

Include an acrylic-only condition and a corresponding condition with a non-zero minor tackifier-like fraction, preferably at matched reactive mass fraction, so H-DUAL can be separated from H-CORE and H-RESIN.

For every tested composition, calculate the frozen H-CORE linear-dilution prediction E1_drift times reactive mass fraction and compare the measured drift both with that prediction and with the H-RESIN threshold of less than half that prediction.
Measure the realized viscosity level at matched temperature and time for each preparation so a change in hold drift is not conflated with uncontrolled realization-state displacement.
If the chemistry audit does not establish shared-shape applicability for a modified candidate, obtain a fresh 80-130 C sweep in 10 C increments rather than relying on one-point state calibration.
planner.scientific_question: At matched reactive mass fraction and hold conditions, do resin-modified E2-anchored compositions reduce 15-60 min viscosity drift only by the linear dilution expected from the reactive core, suppress drift substantially beyond linear dilution, or require a non-zero minor tackifier-like fraction in addition to the acrylic-like modifier to reach the low-drift regime?

proposer.chemistry_support_assessment: S1C41 is resin-modified chemistry outside the family in which the shared temperature-response shape was measured. However, M-HOLD-120 directly observes matched-window drift and does not reconstruct it from that shared shape, so the chemistry audit keeps this card admissible. The result remains subject to moderate preparation-state risk, requiring controlled and recorded process histories.
hypotheses_not_separated: H-RESIN vs H-DUAL cannot be separated because both predict low drift for this dual-axis composition

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 remains below 3.80% across at least two repeats, the drift is less than half the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction. This falsifies H-CORE for this composition and supports superlinear resin-associated suppression. Because both modifier axes are active, the result remains compatible with both H-RESIN and H-DUAL and does not establish that the tackifier is required.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 is at or above 7.61%, H-RESIN is falsified and the predicted low-drift response of H-DUAL at a tackifier-containing composition is also contradicted. Agreement with 7.61% within measurement resolution supports H-CORE's linear-dilution rule.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result above 3.80% but below 7.61% indicates partial suppression that meets neither the registered superlinear acceptance threshold nor the linear-dilution falsification boundary cleanly. Repeat consistency and the 2 percentage-point resolution must be examined, and an acrylic-only matched-reactive-fraction hold would still be needed to distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL.

proposer.primary_observable: Directly measured SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, during a 120 C hold with viscosity recorded at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min across at least two independent repeats.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: Deterministically tied, but it raises acrylic loading to 17.5% and total modifier burden to 22.5% without separating any additional hypothesis pair.
Deterministically tied and located at a directly commensurate 20% acrylic evidence anchor, but its 25% total modifier burden is a larger chemistry departure with no added hypothesis discrimination.
Deterministically tied, but its 27.5% total modifier burden is larger and its predicted H-CORE versus low-drift contrast is smaller than for S1C41.
Deterministically tied, but it uses the largest modifier burden in the tied set, 30%, without gaining pairwise discrimination.
It retains direct drift measurement but uses 7.5% tackifier, outside the repeated 4.8-6.4% support cluster, producing nonzero extrapolation risk and a lower VOI score.

It directly verifies temperature-response shape in the modified chemistry but reads a fitted slope, does not test the declared hot-hold failure mode, and separates none of the registered drift hypotheses.
It would reduce realization-state uncertainty but addresses process repeatability rather than directly separating the registered formulation-level drift mechanisms.

proposer.reasoning: S1C41::M-HOLD-120 has the maximum stable VOI, directly measures the least-resolved and decision-relevant 120 C drift coordinate, and separates two of the three registered hypothesis pairs without relying on an unverified thermal-shape transfer. Its 15% acrylic and 5% tackifier levels remain within the stated supported intervention regions. Within the genuine five-way tie, it is preferred as the minimum-burden intervention, while explicitly acknowledging that a single dual-axis experiment cannot distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL.
proposer.tie_break_justification: All five cards have identical VOI component vectors and place both modifier axes inside the supported regions. S1C41 uses the smallest total modifier burden: 15% acrylic-like modifier plus 5% minor tackifier-like modifier. It therefore makes the smallest justified departure from the characterized reactive core while retaining full axis coverage, zero scored extrapolation risk, and a 3.804 percentage-point separation between the linear-dilution and low-drift predictions, exceeding the 2 percentage-point measurement threshold.

robustness_adjudication.change_from_proposal: Changed from the tied-top dual-axis S1C41::M-HOLD-120 card to the explicitly identified matched-reactive-fraction acrylic-only S1C49::M-HOLD-120 card. This sacrifices deterministic VOI rank to separate H-DUAL from the resin-suppression alternative: low drift without TK100 can formally falsify H-DUAL. M-HOLD-120 remains admissible because it directly observes drift and does not reuse the unsupported shared temperature-response shape.
robustness_adjudication.departure_from_deterministic_ranking: The proposal S1C41::M-HOLD-120 is in the five-card tied deterministic top set. However, the preferred experiment departs from that ranking to S1C49::M-HOLD-120 because the entire top set consists of dual-axis formulations that leave H-RESIN and H-DUAL entangled. S1C49 is the explicitly identified matched-total-modifier acrylic-only candidate at the same reactive mass fraction of 0.8000, and a low-drift result can satisfy the registered falsification condition for H-DUAL. This hypothesis-separation advantage is not captured adequately by the top-set score.
residual_decision_risk: No directly measured unmodified E2-core hold baseline is included, so comparisons with the E1-derived linear-dilution prediction cannot uniquely establish H-CORE versus H-RESIN.
The E1 reference drift is based on one run and its uncertainty is not represented in the nominal 2 percentage-point discrimination comparison.

S1C49 is modified chemistry outside the measured support of the shared temperature-response shape; M-HOLD-120 remains valid, but no temperature-response transfer or one-point reconstruction claim is permissible without a fresh M-SWEEP.
Substantial E2 preparation-state variation remains a confound unless process histories are controlled and recorded across independent preparations.
The repeat aggregation and uncertainty rule must be preregistered before observing results.

A single acrylic-only experiment cannot isolate all modifier, dilution, and interaction effects; a paired S1C41 comparison and an unmodified E2-core control remain necessary for the full scientific question.
Macroscopic viscosity drift cannot establish the proposed molecular encounter-frequency mechanism.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection does not invalidate direct measurement of SI_15_60, but it prevents interpreting deviation from 7.61% as uniquely caused by modifier-induced superlinear suppression. That comparator transfers a single E1 hold result at NCO:OH 1.7 to an E2-anchored formulation at NCO:OH 1.8 without an E2-core hold baseline. An unmodified E2-core control is therefore still required for a valid H-CORE versus H-RESIN attribution. The separate choice of S1C49 over S1C41 is driven by additional hypothesis discrimination: unlike the dual-axis top set, the acrylic-only card can directly test the registered requirement in H-DUAL.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: No tested one-term perturbation changed the tied top set: top_experiment_set_stability was 1.0, no flipped scenarios occurred, and every recommendation_flip_boundary survived scaling from 0.5 to 1.5. Thus none of the reported perturbations makes S1C41 cease to be top ranked. No alternative weighting within the tested sweep can be assessed as scientifically preferable because no flip occurred. The base margin to the first strictly lower experiment was only 0.004583, but that numerical stability does not resolve the unencoded H-RESIN versus H-DUAL entanglement and does not validate the transferred E1 baseline.

skeptic.chemistry_domain_support_assessment: The primary observable stays independent of the shared thermal-response model: S1C41::M-HOLD-120 directly measures 120 C matched-window drift, so it does not reuse the unmodified-family thermal shape outside support. Any claim about temperature-response transfer or reconstruction from an anchor would require a fresh 80-130 C M-SWEEP for S1C41; the binding audit correctly removes the modified-chemistry M-ANCHOR card.
skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The specified hold can produce directly observed drift at or above 7.61% or below 3.80%, so the numeric H-RESIN and H-CORE criteria are measurable in practice. The repeat aggregation rule must be prespecified, and the E1-derived baseline must be replaced or validated with an E2-core hold. This dual-axis protocol cannot satisfy the registry's formal H-DUAL falsification condition because that condition requires an acrylic-only low-drift result.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A result below 3.80% would not cleanly falsify reactive-core scaling or establish suppression beyond the appropriate E2-core dilution baseline.
objections.objection: The claimed H-CORE prediction of 7.61% is calculated as the single-run E1 drift of 9.51% times S1C41's reactive mass fraction of 0.8000, even though E1 has NCO:OH = 1.7 while S1C41 preserves the E2 core at NCO:OH = 1.8. E2 has no measured hold trajectory. Without an unmodified E2-core M-HOLD-120 control, a deviation from 7.61% cannot be assigned uniquely to superlinear resin suppression rather than to a different intrinsic drift coefficient of the E2 reactive core. The nominal 3.804 percentage-point separation exceeds the declared 2.00 percentage-point candidate-measurement resolution, but that comparison omits uncertainty in the single-run E1 reference.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Low drift could only support the joint class of resin-associated suppression explanations; it could not establish that TK100 is required or that acrylic alone would suffice.
objections.objection: S1C41 contains both 15% AC1920 and 5% TK100, and H-RESIN and H-DUAL are both assigned the same 3.804% prediction. The experiment therefore cannot distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL. The Proposer correctly declares this in hypotheses_not_separated and states that an acrylic-only matched-reactive-fraction hold is required.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Claims of tackifier requirement, acrylic-specific action, modifier specialization, or interaction between the two modifiers would be unsupported.
objections.objection: The formulation changes three linked quantities relative to the reactive core: AC1920 is raised to 15%, TK100 is raised to 5%, and reactive-core fraction falls to 0.8000. Because both modifier axes move together in a single composition, the protocol cannot attribute any suppression to AC1920, TK100, an AC1920-by-TK100 interaction, or a modifier-specific effect beyond dilution. It also lacks a same-core, same-reactive-fraction acrylic-only comparator.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The measured drift remains valid, but treating its comparison with 7.61% as equally direct would overstate the strength of the mechanistic evidence.
objections.objection: The primary observable itself survives this attack: SI_15_60 is calculated directly from viscosity measured at 15 and 60 minutes during the specified 120 C hold. It requires no thermal-shape fit, extrapolation, or imputation. However, the interpretation against 7.61% inherits the unsupported E1-to-E2 baseline transfer noted separately.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: No primary drift claim is invalidated, provided no temperature-response or one-point reconstruction claim is added without a direct M-SWEEP.
objections.objection: S1C41 is outside the chemistry family used to establish the shared temperature-response shape, but M-HOLD-120 does not use that shape to reconstruct SI_15_60. The proposal therefore does not reuse the unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI thermal-response shape outside its measured support for the primary observable. The binding audit appropriately leaves S1C41::M-HOLD-120 admissible while excluding S1C41::M-ANCHOR.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A high-drift S1C41 result could be misreported as formally falsifying H-DUAL even though the required acrylic-only observation was never made.
objections.objection: The protocol can directly produce SI_15_60 values at or above 7.61% or below 3.80%, so the numeric H-RESIN and H-CORE decision boundaries are operationally attainable. It cannot, however, meet the registry's formal falsification condition for H-DUAL, which requires an acrylic-only composition to reach low drift without minor tackifier. The statement that a dual-axis result at or above 7.61% falsifies or contradicts H-DUAL is therefore not equivalent to the registered H-DUAL falsification criterion.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Discordant repeats could not be adjudicated reproducibly, making the practical accept/falsify decision dependent on an unstated post-result rule.
objections.objection: The criteria say that thresholds must hold 'across at least two repeats,' but the protocol does not specify whether each repeat must individually cross the threshold, whether the repeat mean is compared with the threshold, or how uncertainty is used. This is important because the declared discrimination resolution is 2.00 percentage points and the E2 realization data show 2.80-3.57-fold viscosity-scale spreads.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A rheological result could be overinterpreted as proof of a specific molecular or encounter-frequency mechanism.
objections.objection: No hidden target result or validation-formulation outcome is used in the stated selection. However, M-HOLD-120 measures only macroscopic viscosity drift and cannot establish the H-RESIN statement that suppression occurs by lowering effective concentration and encounter frequency of reaction-capable species. It can establish phenomenological suppression relative to a valid baseline, not that molecular explanation.

skeptic.recommended_change: Run a paired M-HOLD-120 design under the same recorded process history: S1C41, the matched-total-modifier acrylic-only candidate S1C49 at reactive mass fraction 0.8000, and an unmodified E2-core hold control. Use at least two independent preparations per composition and preregister whether thresholds apply to every repeat or to a repeat mean with a stated uncertainty rule. The E2 control supplies the correct dilution baseline, while S1C41 versus S1C49 isolates whether non-zero TK100 is required.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The 7.61% H-CORE comparator is transferred from a single E1 hold run at NCO:OH = 1.7 to an E2-anchored candidate at NCO:OH = 1.8, even though E2 has no measured hold trajectory. Without a directly measured unmodified E2-core hold baseline, the experiment cannot uniquely attribute deviation from 7.61% to the modifiers.

tool_trace.name: get_chemistry_audited_rheology_summary
tool_trace.reason: Mandatory first action: candidate or experiment ranking is inadmissible until the chemistry-provenance-audited upstream material structure, shared-shape evidence, hold contrast and E1 +P perturbation check are loaded.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The verified E1 +P phosphoric-acid perturbation is excluded from the primary same-composition fit and is interpreted separately as a chemical-perturbation check.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.
Keep deliberately chemistry-perturbed curves outside same-composition fitting, but use them to test whether an intervention shifts viscosity scale, thermal-response shape, or both.

chemical_perturbation_check.interpretation: The verified low-dose H3PO4 perturbation shifts the observed viscosity level while remaining closely compatible with the local shared thermal-response geometry. It is a separate chemical-perturbation check and is not pooled into the primary same-composition state model.

observational_E1_R01_day1_comparator.interpretation_boundary: Observational reference only; the compact record does not establish a paired parent-batch relationship between E1 +P and E1 R01 day-1.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.
experiment_design_implications.verified_acid_perturbation: E1 +P received 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution during dehydration. Its close agreement with the primary shared thermal shape makes it useful as a defined scale-versus-shape perturbation check, not as another nominal E1 realization.

provenance_audit.reason: E1 +P is a verified chemical perturbation: 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution was added during dehydration. It is excluded from the same-composition primary state model and exposed separately as a perturbation check.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

chemistry_applicability_audit.enforcement_note: In this condition the chemistry applicability audit is BINDING. The cards it marks inadmissible were removed before ranking and are not selectable. You may state that you disagree with the rule and why; naming a removed card is an invalid output.
rule_text: Scope: measurement admissibility, not formulation admissibility.
M-HOLD-120, M-REPEAT and M-SWEEP observe their quantity directly and remain admissible.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use == 'allowed_with_state_anchor', or when a versioned prior direct sweep has verified transferability for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification: the one-point anchor would reconstruct 120-130 C viscosity through a shape that has never been measured for that chemistry.
This audit is a deterministic scientific rule, not a VOI penalty and not a model opinion. Whether it is binding in this run is stated by the enforcement field.

voi.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.

top_cards.falsification_criterion: H-RESIN is falsified if matched 15-60 min drift is at or above the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61%. This composition carries both axes, so it cannot separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL; an acrylic-only hold is the follow-up required for that.
